newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: France's Chirac seeks trade boost on Argentine tour.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac seeks trade boost on Argentine tour.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac began a two-day state visit to Argentina on Monday, winding up a five-nation tour of Latin America in France's closest economic and cultural partner in the region.

Chirac, on a tour designed to boost relations between the four-nation South American Mercosur customs union and the European Union, was having talks with President Carlos Menem at the Casa Rosada presidential palace on Monday morning.

Earlier, during an official welcome by Foreign Minister Guido di Tella, Chirac voiced hopes that his visit would give "a fresh and powerful impulse" to bilateral relations that had been loosened through Argentina's military dictatorship in the 1970s and economic crisis in the 1980s.

"Our political, economic and cultural relations are not yet up to the deep affinities that have always linked our people," he said. He said his trip, beyond seeking to boost business with Argentina, was "a visit from the heart".

To highlight cultural links between the countries, Chirac has taken on his tour Argentine-born writer Hector Bianciotti, who was recently elected to the French Academy, guardians of the French language.
In a speech at Menem's office, Chirac pointed to the two countries' common economic and political interests and hailed Argentina's return to democracy and respect for human rights.

Relations were long soured by the kidnapping of two French nuns by former navy Capt. Alfredo Astiz during Argentina's "dirty war" against suspected leftists in the 1970s. Astiz, still under an international arrest warrant from French justice, retired from the navy last year and Menem promised during a state visit to France last year to compensate the relatives of the nuns.

French officials say France has become the largest single investor in Argentina since it restored economic stability and ended runaway inflation in the early 1990s. French companies have heavily invested in Argentina's privatisation of utilities and telecommunications, oil, agriculture, medicine and chemicals.
Renault and Peugeot-Citroen hold a third of the car market.

Eager to boost trade with the region and alleviate France's record unemployment, Chirac made his week-long trip to Mercosur members Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina, plus Bolivia, with dozens of French business leaders in tow. He urged them to seize major business opportunities from the growth of Mercosur, which he called the world's fourth strongest economic power.
